newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt corruption squad to hold public-sector boss.
newsitem.headline: Egypt corruption squad to hold public-sector boss.

text.p: Egypt's anti-corruption squad has ordered a former public-sector boss detained for 15 days for questioning on allegations he took millions of dollars in commissions, the government newspaper al-Akhbar said on Wednesday.
The official, Abdelwahhab el-Habbak, was chairman of the Holding Company for Engineering Industries until May.

The detention order came from the Illegal Gains Department, which investigates official corruption, al-Akhbar said. It said investigations into the case were almost complete and the results would be made public within days.
Officials at the department were not immediately available to comment on the case on Wednesday.
Another government newspaper, al-Gomhuria, said police detained Habbak on Tuesday. A servant at his house said on Wednesday he was at home in the morning but later went out.

The opposition newspaper al-Wafd on Tuesday quoted Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri as saying Habbak had offered to repay $19 million he had deposited in Swiss bank accounts. The Egyptian authorities asked for more but Habbak refused.
"The prime minister said he had not and would not cover up corruption and there would be no protection for any official who tampers with public money, whatever his position," it added.
The Holding Company for Engineering Industries is parent company to 21 state manufacturing firms, several of which are listed for early privatisation.
